extentRule.measured: Every vertex of the package's geometry-valid features is transformed (pyproj, always_xy, allow_ballpark=False, only_best=True) from the declared CRS to EPSG:4326 and to the analysis CRS; extents are shapely bounds of the transformed shapes. Analysis CRS is the area reference's analysisCrs when the area has one, else WGS 84 UTM of the package's geographic middle (zone floor((lon+180)/6)+1, 326xx if lat>=0 else 327xx).
rules: line 467: EPSG:4326 extent within -180..180 lon and -80..84 lat, at most 1 degree each way
line 473: middle of the extent inside the analysis CRS area of use, longitude give or take 0.25 degree
line 478: extent in analysis metres at most MAX_EXTENT_M = 50000 m each way (strictly greater refuses)
line 486: every edge within 50000 m of the area origin (the area reference's origin, else the package's south-west corner)
extentRule.units: degrees for rule 467, metres in the analysis UTM zone for 478 and 486

facts.allCutsOneArea: Every cut of one file is drafted into one destination area (intakeCaseArea or the file seed key, intake-large-worker largeDestination). The first package fixes that area's analysisCrs and origin (areas.ts persistPreparedAreaImport), so area.py line 486 refuses any later package more than 50 km from that origin whatever the cut size.
facts.unfinishedPackageLimit: INTAKE_UNFINISHED_PACKAGE_LIMIT = 8 (intake-part-draft.ts). draftCut returns 'pressure' at 8 unreviewed packages and step() skips drafting until an intake run's automatic review wakes the file; the row showed 'reading' with no words. There is no limit on the total number of packages.

design: intake-package-extent.ts (new): AREA_NORMALIZER_EXTENT mirrors area.py lines 35/467/473/478/486; measurableCrs reads the crs member as _geojson_crs does (none, CRS84, EPSG:4326, EPSG:3857, WGS 84 UTM); utmForward/utmInverse are the 6th-order Krüger series PROJ uses for UTM.

CutExtent.admit adds a feature only if the whole cut still passes all four rules, in the area's analysis zone and origin when the area has a reference, else in the cut's own middle zone and south-west corner; a feature already in the target zone keeps its own coordinates, as PROJ's no-op.

IntakePackageCutter(metadata, resume, frame) closes the cut before a feature that fails the extent, and holds a feature that fails alone: PART_FEATURE_EXTENT_BOUND (wider than any area) or PART_FEATURE_AREA_BOUND (outside this area). No feature is split, moved or simplified. A system or analysis CRS this module cannot convert exactly leaves cuts on size alone, as before.

intake-large-worker reads the destination area's stored reference into the fold; a step that starts without one ends after its first cut, so every later cut is made in the stored reference both in one run and on resume. Part counts gain heldWide and heldOutside beside held.

intake-large.ts words: end summary counts wide and outside holds in their own sentences; the drafting row at the unfinished limit says '8 packages of this file wait for review. The rest of the file is cut into packages as these are reviewed.'

limits: Area binding is unchanged: one destination area per file, so features more than 50 km from its origin are held (Halifax: 13395 of 172409) instead of stopping the import. Mapping them needs one area per spatial cell (AUD2 'real fix', intake-destination.ts); that is the lead's call.

Spatially scattered files make many small packages: Halifax in file order gives 2778 packages averaging 57 features, each normalized and reviewed by the intake run 8 at a time. A windowed spatial partition (several open cuts per bounded window of the file, resume from the window start recorded in the part locator) would cut this by an order of magnitude; not built here.

Measured systems: no crs, CRS84, EPSG:4326, EPSG:3857, WGS 84 UTM (32601-32660, 32701-32760). Any other declared system, or an area analysis CRS other than WGS 84 UTM (for example EPSG:6933), keeps the size-only cuts and area.py's refusal words.

TypeScript measures every feature, area.py only geometry-valid ones; the TypeScript extent is therefore never smaller. For a cut without a reference whose rejected features move its middle across a zone line, the zones can differ; the metric difference is below 0.1 % and matters only within about 50 m of the 50 km limit.
A feature with no convertible position (for example an out-of-range longitude) is held as wider than one area; area.py would refuse its whole part.
